title: Signal Garrison release brief and day-of shift cheatsheet
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact day-of ops brief for the "Signal Garrison" launch lane. Focus: keep the release small but observability-complete — strong telemetry gates, explicit comm ladder, and clear rollforward/rollback cues. Use this as the single-page cheat during the 72h watch.

Summary (one-line):
Incremental release of inference-routing v2 (traffic-split + KV-cache tuning + kernel selection tweak) to 10% canary in us-west-2, then staggered ramp to 50% paired regional fallback. Goal: validate latency P50/P95, error spike behavior, and cost-per-token drift.

Quick facts:
- Release name: signal-garrison-2027-06
- Components: routing-api, serving-runtime (kv cache), kernel-selector service
- Canary window: 2027-06-14 09:00 UTC -> initial 3h observation -> expansion plan
- Initial canary percentage: 10% of baseline traffic (sticky by session)
- Target regions: us-west-2 -> eu-west-1 (staggered)
- Owner (day-of): Aisha P (ops lead), Miguel O (runtime), Lin C (telemetry lead)

Day-of timeline (compressed):
- -24h (preflight): final smoke on staging, config diff signed, quick sanity runbook checklist done 
- -2h: shift handover: oncall reassured, comm channel created (#release-signal-garrison), pager rotations posted
- T0 (09:00 UTC): flip traffic at control plane to 10% canary; validate health checks green
- T0 + 15m: latency sanity check (p50/p95) — compare to baseline snapshot
- T0 + 60m: check error budget and 429/5xx funnel; verify no stealth amplification in async queues
- T0 + 180m: decision point -> expand to 25% or rollback to 0% (see gating rules)
- T0 + 12h: if stable, expand to 50% for 6h observation then full ramp plan starts next day

Telemetry & gating rules (telemetry lead -> Lin):
- Primary signals (auto-monitored):
  - p50 latency (text-gen): +10% from baseline -> INFO (continue watch)
  - p95 latency: +20% -> ALERT (investigate, consider throttle)
  - error rate (5xx + downstream 4xx): >0.5% of requests -> WARNING
  - client-visible incorrect outputs (from regression eval pipeline): any regression >1% on watch prompts -> CRITICAL
  - cost-per-token (rolling 1h): +15% -> investigate quantization path fallthroughs
- Escalation thresholds:
  - Auto-rollback trigger: p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes OR sustained 5xx rate >1% for 5 minutes
  - Manual rollback recommended: unexplained model-quality regressions, or downstream backpressure in embeddings-service
  - Soft-throttle: reduce batch size / increase async queue processing if p95 drift between +20% and +100% but errors <0.5%
- Tagging: all canary requests get header X-Canary: signal-garrison-2027-06 for trace filtering

Operational checklist (preflight -> day-of):
- Preflight (owners: infra + release-eng):
  - Verify infra quotas in us-west-2 (gpu slots >= expected peak)
  - Confirm rollback images are built and tested (images: runtime:v2.6-rollback, routing:v2.1-rollback)
  - KV-cache warmup script included in rollout plan and smoke tests
  - Canary routing policy uploaded and validated in control plane UI
  - Observability dashboards created (canary vs baseline panes) and annotated
- Day-of (owners: ops lead + runtime):
  - Start one-line comm in #release-signal-garrison, create ephemeral huddle call
  - Flip 10% canary; verify 200s at endpoint for synthetic smoke probes
  - Confirm traces include X-Canary header and KV-cache span tags
  - Validate autoscaler not triggered unexpectedly (scale events logged)
  - Run targeted eval set (100 prompts) through canary endpoints and compare to baseline diff tool
- Post-expand (owners: product + eng):
  - Update release notes draft with observed KPIs (latency, errors, regressions)
  - Create follow-up tickets for fixes if any regressions observed

Communication ladder (who to ping when):
- INFO (nonblocking anomalies): post to #release-signal-garrison, ping telemetry lead (Lin)
- WARNING (potentially blocking): page runtime lead (Miguel) and ops lead (Aisha)
- CRITICAL (immediate rollback): page SRE lead, oncall-platform, and product manager — all-hands huddle within 5 minutes

Rollback / rollforward playbook (short):
- Rollback steps:
  1) Shift canary traffic to baseline (control plane toggle) -> confirm 0% traffic to new variant
  2) Redeploy previous stable runtime image if control-plane toggle not sufficient
  3) Notify customers in affected region via status page if user-visible failures detected
  4) Open incident in PagerDuty and tag with release name
- Rollforward steps (after rollback investigation):
  1) Fix hotpatch (if minor) and run short dry-run with synthetic load in staging
  2) Re-initiate canary at 5% for longer observation window
  3) If rollforward repeatedly fails, demote feature behind runtime flag and keep stable kernel selection

Canary expansion decision matrix (T0 + 3h):
- If all primary signals within thresholds -> expand to 25%
- If p95 latency borderline (between +20% and +100%) but error rate <0.5% -> hold at 10% for additional 3h and rerun evals
- If any auto-rollback trigger hit -> rollback immediately

Night watch & 72h stabilization notes:
- After a successful 50% window and no critical regressions for 24h, ops to handoff to steady-state oncall
- 72h post-release: consolidate final telemetry, run full regression eval (5k prompts), and publish release notes
- If medium-severity regressions observed in first 72h, schedule hotfix sprint and delay full ramp

Draft release notes (to be expanded post-rollout):
- headline: Improved routing heuristics reduce tail latency for short prompts by up to 12% in initial canary; KV-cache warmup included.
- details: Kernel-selector now prefers fused attention kernels for shorter sequences — measurable p50 gains and slight p95 tradeoff in edge cases; we are monitoring and have throttle knobs ready.
- known issues: Under certain burst patterns, autoscaler scale-ups can introduce transient 5xxs for <2m; mitigations: tweaked readiness probe and backoff config queued.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we use circuit-breaker per-customer during canary to protect heavy tenants? (ask platform team)
- Add an automated synthetic that exercises the KV-cache cold/warm path every 10 mins for first 12h
- Confirm with legal if EU telemetry retention window is ok for canary traces in eu-west-1

Sign-offs needed prior to rollout (checklist):
- [ ] Security review for new header propagation and trace tags (sec)
- [ ] Capacity confirmation (infra)
- [ ] PM acceptance on quality threshold for canary (product)
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards validated (telemetry)

Field notes & heuristics (operational tips):
- Warm the KV-cache with low-cost synthetic before flipping traffic to avoid first-request penalty cascade
- Keep a short list of safe fallback model ids in the routing service (fast switch if quality regressions spike)
- When rolling back: prefer control-plane traffic flip first — it is fastest and least disruptive when sticky sessions can be rebalanced

Appendix: quick commands (for oncall)
- Flip canary to 10%: ./control-plane toggle --name signal-garrison-2027-06 --percent 10
- Force rollback to baseline: ./control-plane toggle --name signal-garrison-2027-06 --percent 0 && kubectl set image deployment/runtime runtime=runtime:v2.5-stable
- Pull canary traces: curl -H 'X-Canary: signal-garrison-2027-06' https://observability.internal/api/traces?since=1h

End of brief — keep this doc pinned in the channel during the release. Any additions, ping me and I will fold into post-release notes.
